Physics: All three keys check out (λ = 0.40 m and v = ω/k = 4.0 m s⁻¹; ΔV = 1.2×10⁻⁵ m³ = 12 mL; v_rms ratio = √(2/32) = 1:4), the data are complete and consistent, and the distractors are well-targeted at common slips (using k as λ, forgetting the √ in the rms formula, unit conversion). However, every item is a single-formula substitution solvable in 20–30 s, so the section is uniformly at the easy end and lacks any conceptual or two-step problem. Adding one item requiring reasoning (e.g. phase/particle-velocity in waves, or a degrees-of-freedom/mixture question in kinetic theory) would bring the difficulty spread closer to a real BITSAT paper.

Chemistry: The three items span p-block hydrolysis, crystal-field/spin-state reasoning and ether cleavage, giving reasonable topical spread, and the keys for Q4 and Q5 are chemically sound. The level is on the easy side — Q4 is pure NCERT recall and Q5 is a standard weak-field/strong-field comparison — so a slightly more application-based item would improve balance. Q6 is the only blocker: its structure-bearing figure is absent, and its two "SN2 at the aromatic carbon" distractors are mechanistically impossible, leaving effectively a two-option choice even once the figure is restored.

[major] The figure referred to by "The ether shown" is not supplied, so the structure cannot be checked against the options (which presuppose tert-butyl p-tolyl ether); the item must be re-issued with the structure drawn or named explicitly in the stem.
